classification.difficultyReason: Construct a minimum spanning tree from a specified starting vertex and interpret its total weight as pipe length.

content.prompt:
Water is to be piped from a water tank to seven outlets.
The possible pipe connections are shown. The distances, in km, are shown as edge weights.

spec.description: Eight marked vertices and twelve weighted undirected edges. Outlet G subdivides the A-to-E route; Outlet C subdivides the Tank-to-B route. Ordinary edges, markers and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: AB=13, A–Tank=11, AG=6, AF=12, GE=10, FE=7, E–Tank=8, ED=9, Tank–D=5, Tank–C=2, CB=6, BD=11; weights are kilometres.
spec.answerVisibility: All network givens remain visible; no selected spanning-tree edges are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Starting at the tank, construct the minimum spanning tree.

answer.short: Tank–C, Tank–D, C–B, Tank–E, E–F, E–G and G–A.
answer.worked: Starting at the tank, successively select the least-weight edge connecting the current tree to a new vertex: Tank–C (2), Tank–D (5), C–B (6), Tank–E (8), E–F (7), E–G (10), G–A (6). All eight vertices are connected by seven edges with no cycle.

spec.description: Complete minimum spanning tree retaining the source vertex positions, outlet labels and selected edge weights.
spec.mathematics: Selected edges: Tank–C 2, Tank–D 5, C–B 6, Tank–E 8, E–F 7, E–G 10, G–A 6.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the minimum length of pipe required?
